workstreams.title: Set up the tiddl CLI
workstreams.body: # Set up the tiddl CLI Install and OAuth-authenticate the tiddl CLI (github.com/oskvr37/tiddl) and verify it downloads TIDAL albums in LOSSLESS quality, replacing the dead download-album.js proxy path.

workstreams.title: Monochrome.tf Pre-Coding Research Phase
workstreams.body: ## Purpose **This workstream must be completed before any planning (WS-6, WS-7, WS-8 plans) or spec tasks are written.** The goal is to use Playwright to actually visit `monochrome.tf`, inspect its behavior, capture network traffic, and document everything the automation tool will need to know. **No code will be written during this phase.** Only observation, documentation, and evidence gathering.

workstreams.title: Node v2 of download-album.js driving the monochrome.tf UI with real Chrome
workstreams.body: Rebuild download-album.js as a Node v2 that drives the monochrome.tf web UI with Playwright + the user's real Chrome, so Turnstile passes and real FLAC downloads complete — replacing the dead direct-API approach.

workstreams.title: Batch runner script that reads an album/artist list file and calls download-album-v2 per line
workstreams.body: A second script that reads a list file of volumes (Roman-numeral sets) and album/artist lines, loops through each entry, and invokes download-album-v2.js for each — with per-volume output folders and a final summary of exit codes.

workstreams.title: Add FFmpeg HE-AAC recompression stage to the batch runner
workstreams.body: Add an FFmpeg recompression step to download-album-list.js that re-encodes each downloaded album's audio into Minichrome HE-AAC 64k m4a files, mirroring the manual find+ffmpeg command from /Volumes/T7/Downloads/SpotifyExodus/README.md. The user's manual workflow: after downloading an album, run `find ./<Album> -type f \( -iname "*.flac" -o -iname "*.mp3" \)` and re-encode each file with `ffmpeg -i <in> -vn -c:a libfdk_aac -profile:a aac_he -b:a 64k <out>.m4a` into a Minichrome folder. The new runner must do this per album after its download completes. The recompression output folder is ours to choose — a sibling of the download folder (e.g. `<base>/<Volume N>/Minichrome/<artist>/<album>/` or similar), per-volume to stay self-contained. Decisions and constraints from analysis (do not re-litigate):

workstreams.title: Automated MusicBrainz metadata tagging of recompressed files
workstreams.body: Automate the manual MusicBrainz Picard step: match and update metadata on the recompressed HE-AAC files so they import cleanly into music players. Today the user manually drags each recompressed album's files into MusicBrainz Picard on macOS to match and update metadata before import into players, because the source FLACs carry little metadata and it does not carry across into the recompressed m4a files. This must become an automated step of the download pipeline. Research conclusion (do not re-litigate): MusicBrainz Picard itself has no true headless mode — a feature request (PICARD-3100) is open, and its `-e` executable commands (LOAD/LOOKUP/SAVE_MATCHED) still boot the full GUI. The recommended path is beets as a headless autotagger: `beet import -q` with in-place tagging config (`copy: no`, quiet fallback, strong_rec_thresh) matches via the same MusicBrainz + AcoustID machinery and writes tags into m4a directly.

workstreams.title: Separate FLAC and recompressed output bases for the batch runner
workstreams.body: Give download-album-list.js two explicit output bases instead of one base plus a hardcoded "Minichrome" subfolder. The user's real library lives as two sibling trees on an external drive: flacs under /Volumes/T7/Downloads/SpotifyExodus/Monochrome and recompressed/matched files under /Volumes/T7/Downloads/SpotifyExodus/Minichrome. The current runner emits flacs at <base>/<Volume N>/<artist>/<album> and m4as at <base>/<Volume N>/Minichrome/<artist>/<album> — verified NOT nested (sibling trees under the volume root), but the "Minichrome" name is hardcoded and there is no way to send the recompressed output to a different base (e.g. a different drive or the legacy Minichrome folder). Requested behaviour:

workstreams.title: Reorganize legacy SpotifyExodus Monochrome and Minichrome trees by volume
workstreams.body: Reorganize the user's EXISTING legacy download trees on the external drive into the new per-volume layout, matching what the new download-album-list.js runner now produces. Target (NOT the project folder): - FLACs: /Volumes/T7/Downloads/SpotifyExodus/Monochrome — 206 artist directories, each holding album folders

workstreams.title: Reorganize legacy SpotifyExodus trees by volume using Spotify CSV exports
workstreams.body: Reorganize the user's EXISTING legacy download trees on the external drive using **per-playlist Spotify playlist-export CSVs** as the authoritative source of truth (replacing the text list from WS-16). Every CSV becomes a top-level **compilation folder** — no "Volume" concept, no first-volume rule, no non-volume special case. Target (same as WS-16, unchanged): - FLACs: /Volumes/T7/Downloads/SpotifyExodus/Monochrome (206 artist dirs)

workstreams.title: CSV playlist export support for download-album-list with per-volume output layout
workstreams.body: User wants to modify `download-album-list.js` and `download-album-v2.js` to process Exportify CSV playlist exports (one file per volume, `fluid_tracks_volume_i.csv` through `x.csv`) instead of/in addition to the current plain-text `# Volume <roman>` + one-album-per-line format. FLAC files should be saved to Monochrome and recompressed m4a files to Minichrome, both using the new per-volume directory structure `<base>/<Volume N>/<artist>/<album>/` that matches the layout produced by the reorganize-legacy-by-volume script (WS-16). Ten CSV exports exist at `/Volumes/T7/Downloads/SpotifyExodus/exportify/`. The user wants this done as a full pipeline: investigate → plan → spec tasks → execute, with no gates.

workstreams.title: Move Playwright browser window off-screen during download-album-v2 runs
workstreams.body: The download-album-v2 script uses Playwright to spawn a visible desktop browser window for performance actions, then closes it repeatedly. Headless mode doesn't work for the target site. The browser window interrupts the user's workflow while running. The goal is to launch the browser off-screen (using `--window-position=-10000,-10000` in Playwright args) so it runs without blocking the user's desktop, while keeping it fully functional (non-headless).

workstreams.title: Organize the Monochrome archive by volume
workstreams.body: # Organize the Monochrome archive by volume Reorganize the Monochrome lossless archive from the flat Artist/Album layout into Volume I-VIII folders under Monochrome/, matching the volume headers in the Fluid Tracks album list.

workstreams.title: Fix re-download and search-match bugs in monochrome.tf downloader
workstreams.body: download-album-list.js and download-album-v2.js have two bugs: a fragile parseAlbumDirFromStdout regex that returns null on trailing whitespace, and card title extraction that picks up extra DOM text. 1. parseAlbumDirFromStdout regex is fragile — trailing whitespace/carriage returns cause it to return null, breaking album tracking and causing re-downloads 2. Card title extraction may include extra DOM text from nested elements, causing the normalized comparison to fail when searching for albums

workstreams.title: Fix monochrome.tf search query format to include artist alongside album
workstreams.body: The download-album-v2.js search resolver sends "Album - Artist" verbatim to the monochrome.tf search box. The site's search algorithm treats " - " as a significant operator that splits or penalises the query, causing albums like "Hurry up, We're Dreaming - M83" to not be found. Searching with album and artist concatenated by spaces (no dash) resolves the issue.

workstreams.title: Fix ReferenceError: normalizeForMatch is not defined in page.$$eval browser context
workstreams.body: The monochrome.tf album downloader (`download-album-v2.js`) defines `normalizeForMatch` as a Node.js function at line 69, but calls it inside `page.$$eval()` at line 282 — a function that executes in the browser page context. Playwright throws `ReferenceError: normalizeForMatch is not defined`, causing the album search to fail for affected entries. The `addInitScript` injection (lines 226-229) does not define this function for the page context.

workstreams.title: Investigate false-positive skips and 'nothing to download' failures in album download pipeline
workstreams.body: Some albums in the `fluid_tracks_volume_i` playlist are skipped with "already contains N audio file(s)" when they should download, and others open the browser, search, find the album on monochrome.tf, but report "nothing to download" without actually downloading. Console output shows 10 failures all with `ReferenceError: normalizeForMatch is not defined`. User visually confirmed at least two albums (including "Mister Mellow" by Washed Out and "Hurry up, We're Dreaming" by M83) where the browser window flashed and disappeared without downloading. Investigation needed to determine root cause of both skip and failure modes.

workstreams.title: Albums already present on disk are re-downloaded after skip check regression
workstreams.body: After the last fix (WS-22/WS-23), "Mister Mellow" by Washed Out was downloaded again despite already existing at `/Volumes/T7/Downloads/SpotifyExodus/Monochrome/fluid_tracks_volume_i/Washed Out/Mister Mellow`. The user ran the script again and this album — which is already in the target directory — started downloading. Need to investigate why the skip check failed to detect the existing album.

workstreams.title: Album downloads not saving to destination folder and skipping recompression
workstreams.body: The app was downloading albums (e.g., M83) but they were not appearing in the expected destination subfolder (e.g., `fluid_tracks_volume_i`), and the app was skipping recompression entirely. User ran an initial investigation that got stuck in endless thinking loops. The request is to investigate the app fully from top to bottom, trace the call graph, verify destination folders are being read properly and adhered to throughout the app. Key files mentioned: `download-album-list.js` (runner), `download-album-v2.js` (downloader), `monochrome-bundle.js`. The app downloads ZIPs, extracts them, and should recompress audio files into the destination volume folder. Something breaks in the path resolution or file movement between download and recompression.

workstreams.title: Chrome shows unsupported --no-sandbox warning banner when Playwright opens it for album downloads
workstreams.body: Chrome shows "You are using an unsupported command-line flag: --no-sandbox. Stability and security will suffer." in a banner across the top of the Chrome window, just under the location bar, when Playwright launches Chrome to download an album. Origin of the flag is unknown as of now — worth recording on the board for later triage, not a confirmed defect. The --no-sandbox flag disables Chrome's sandbox, so the banner flags a real security/stability tradeoff as well as being visual noise in what is meant to be an off-screen automated browser. No fix is requested yet — this is backlog only. Context a later triage cannot discover for itself:

workstreams.title: Record albums that were not found during downloads to a manifest file in the destination FLAC folder
workstreams.body: Record albums that the downloader could not find or failed to download, so they can be attempted again by other means. Save the record as a file inside the destination FLAC folder (the volume root that download-album-list.js writes into, e.g. `/Volumes/T7/Downloads/SpotifyExodus/Monochrome/fluid_tracks_volume_i`). The point is a durable, human-readable list of the albums that were not found, so nothing falls through the cracks and each one can later be fetched another way. Create a new workstream, investigate the codebase to determine the best way to implement this, then author spec tasks. No execute or commit in the initial request — the user asked for the workstream, the investigation, and spec tasks, then to wait.

workstreams.body: # Automated batch TIDAL downloader Drive tiddl from the Fluid Tracks album list to batch-download the remaining LOSSLESS albums automatically, skipping archived ones, into the volume-organized Monochrome layout.

workstreams.title: Python CLI for Antra FLAC downloads via Playwright
workstreams.body: Build a lightweight Python CLI that uses Playwright to automate Antra's website (antra.hoshi.cfd) — accepts Spotify/Apple Music links, logs in via UI, submits links through the browser, selects download format, initiates processing, monitors progress, and saves the final ZIP file of lossless FLAC tracks, replacing the dead Node.js TIDAL downloader.

workstreams.title: Playwright browser automation for monochrome.tf
workstreams.body: Automate a headless browser session against monochrome.tf to pass the Cloudflare Turnstile challenge, exchange the token for a JWT via the auth endpoint, and maintain a Bearer-authenticated playback API session.

workstreams.title: CLI for downloading tracks and albums from monochrome.tf
workstreams.body: Download tracks and albums from monochrome.tf. Investigating whether the original download-album.js can work against the new endpoints, or whether the Playwright UI path is required.

workstreams.title: FLAC metadata extraction and tagging
workstreams.body: Extract available metadata from monochrome.tf playback responses and write it into the downloaded FLAC files using mutagen — cover art download and embedding, Vorbis comment population for title, artist, album, ISRC, and duration, with album-art caching to avoid redundant fetches.
